Subject: Private DNS & TLS validation for Stellar Data private deployment

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We're starting the final validation before the on-prem edge cutover and want to confirm a minimal checklist from Redwood's side so our security team can sign off. High-level asks:

- Which FQDNs must we delegate into the split-horizon zone vs keep in our on-prem DNS?
- Expected TLS chain (root/intermediate) and whether Redwood will provide a client trust bundle or we should ingest an intermediate into our HSM.
- mTLS expectations for client authentication: do you require mutual TLS from clients in our VPC or only for admin calls?
- OCSP/CRL availability and recommended caching TTLs for low-latency regions.

Attached are our current zone diffs and the CSR samples the edge appliance produced. Can you also confirm any SNI mapping rules Redwood needs for multi-tenant hostnames?

We'd like to get this into your recommended-template so our auditors can close the ticket by Friday.

Thanks,
Alex Reed
IT Ops — Stellar Data
(attachment: zone-diff-20280406.csv, csr-samples.txt)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reed <it_ops@stellardata.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-07T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Private DNS & TLS validation for Stellar Data private deployment

Hi Alex —

Appreciate the clear asks. I've sketched a concise validation checklist (attached: stellar-tls-checklist.pdf) but summary below so your auditors have a quick read:

1) FQDN ownership and split-horizon
   - Delegate the "private.stellar" zone into a stub/forward from Redwood's resolver for runtime lookups of internal endpoints (we only need A/AAAA and SRV for edge discovery).
   - Keep any hostnames used by internal admin consoles wholly under your on-prem authoritative NS (no delegation).

2) Certificate chain and trust
   - Redwood will present a chain terminating at our intermediate (Redwood Edge Intermediate CA). We will provide the intermediate cert and the chain bundle for your CA store.
   - For HSM ingestion: you only need to import the intermediate and the root anchor (we will not push private keys).

3) mTLS
   - Mutual TLS is required for service-to-service calls across the private tunnel and for the internal admin API. Public customer traffic does not use mTLS unless explicitly configured.
   - Client certs are leaf certificates mapped to tenant IDs via SAN OU mapping. We will provide a mapping CSV template; you must ensure CN/SANs on your side match the CSR samples you already sent.

4) OCSP/CRL and availability
   - OCSP stapling is enabled on the edge; Redwood will maintain an OCSP responder with 5s caching at the edge and recommend client-side TTL of 60s for OCSP responses. CRL not required unless you have long-lived certs.

5) SNI and multi-tenant mapping
   - SNI must match the requested tenant FQDN. For wildcard tenants we accept wildcard SANs but prefer explicit SANs for auditability.

Next steps: Can Laura take point on generating the intermediate bundle and Marissa align the SNI mapping playbook? If you can confirm the audit items your security team needs verbatim we can re-run this checklist as a signed evidence pack.

Thanks — attaching the checklist for your auditors.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Manager, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference
(attachment: stellar-tls-checklist.pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reed <it_ops@stellardata.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-08T08:43:00Z
Subject: Re: Private DNS & TLS validation for Stellar Data private deployment

Alex —

Quick technical notes following Stephanie's checklist:

- Zone delegation: We recommend a stub zone on Stellar's on-prem resolvers pointing to our VPC resolver IPs. Avoid full NS delegation for "private.stellar" to reduce blast radius; stub is sufficient for runtime SRV lookups.

- SNI mapping table: attach sample mapping (inlined below) — tenant-id -> sni-fqdn -> cert-sans. We'll push a CSV template in the evidence pack.

- CSR mismatch you sent: one CSR uses CN=edge.internal.stellar (not allowed). Please regenerate with CN matching the tenant FQDN and SAN entries for both IP and dnsName where applicable. See csr-samples.txt row 2.

- Emergency rollback: If you need to revert edge certs, Redwood supports pinning a backup intermediate for 48h; we will coordinate a short window for your ops team to clear their resolver caches (we provide an invalidation script).

Fyi I'm scheduling a 30-min tech sync tomorrow to walk through the stub zone and CSR corrections.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference

2) For stub delegation, can you provide the four resolver IPs for your VPC cluster? We need them for our stub config and firewall rules.

Also, security asked for evidence of OCSP stapling behavior under load — can Redwood provide a short perf log or example output? If not, a signed statement of configuration will suffice for our compliance ticket.

I've attached the zone diff you requested earlier. We're good for the 09:30 sync tomorrow.
